paragraphs: The ML500 was the flagship non-AMG V8 of the M-Class range across two generations. The W163 generation (1997-2005) uses the M113 - a 5.0-litre V8 that was Mercedes' mainstay V8 of that era. From 2005, the W164-generation ML500 switched to the M273, a 5.5-litre V8 that's a different unit entirely, not an evolution of the earlier engine. Knowing which one your car has matters, because the components and rebuild specifics differ between them - which is exactly why we confirm your exact engine by registration before quoting.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every ML500 on the road.

cards.body: A 5.0-litre V8 petrol fitted to the ML500 from 1997 to 2005. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every M113 rebuild.
A 5.5-litre V8 petrol fitted to the ML500 from 2005 to 2011. We replace timing chains, bearings and gaskets as standard on every M273 rebuild.

compatibility.intro: Because the ML500 spans two distinct V8 engines across two generations, fitting the wrong replacement - or assuming an M113 part will work on an M273 car - risks a compatibility problem that's expensive to unpick. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm:

points.text: Your exact engine code (M256) via registration or VIN
Any electronics or ECU considerations specific to your exact build

compatibility.footer: This is why we always start with your registration rather than a generic M-Class quote - it protects you from paying for parts that don't fit your actual car.
